deities: Tripura Sundari (Raj Rajeshwari, form of Durga/Shakti) - the idol is said to have emerged from the ground

history.dynasty: Kalchuri dynasty - built by Kalchuri king Karndev (also named as King Lakshmikarna in one source). An inscription found in the temple complex confirms the 11th-century construction.
history.period: 11th century (c. 1000+ years old per a video report). LEGEND (verify): one news report (obnews.co) says the temple was established in the 7th century and the idol is ~1600 years old, with religious beliefs linking its presence to the Dwapar Yuga and to Danveer Karna of the Mahabharata, whose kuldevi it is said to be. A popular legend says King Karndev offered oil to the goddess and received gold equal to its weight in return. The temple is a known centre of tantra/tantric practice (per visitor accounts; verify).
history.summary: CSV TOWN NOTE: the CSV town 'Jabalpur' is approximate - the temple is at Hathiyagarh in Tewar village on Bhedaghat road, about 13 km from Jabalpur city (town corrected to Tewar); it is about 5 km off the main road (per 99mustsee.com). Built in the 11th century by the Kalchuri king Karndev, the Tripur Sundari Temple is one of the notable Shakti temples of the Jabalpur region, dedicated to Goddess Tripura Sundari (Raj Rajeshwari), 'the beautiful goddess of the three cities'. The idol is said to have emerged from the ground and is revered as self-manifested. Inscriptions in the complex confirm the Kalchuri-era construction, and the goddess is the kuldevi (family deity) of the Kalchuris in local tradition. Devotees visit year-round, with the biggest crowds during Navratri; photography is not allowed inside the temple (per templetravel.info).

name: Tripur Sundari Temple (Tewar)
town_description: Tewar is a village on the Bhedaghat road (NH 12), about 13 km from Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. The temple stands at Hathiyagarh near Tewar, in a natural setting said to enhance its beauty; pincode 483053.
